Transcript:
[00:00] Alex (AE): Hey everyone thanks for joining, Alex from Redwood here, I'm gonna kick us off. Can you hear me okay?
[00:06] Maria: Yep loud and clear.
[00:08] Jin: Good, thanks. We have about an hour.
[00:10] Alex: Awesome. Quick round robin — I'll pass to Samir in a sec to go over the technical bit, but high level agenda: map MSA/DPA exceptions, agree SLA targets, discuss hosted vs dedicated capacity and pricing, KMS/egress, then next steps. Anything to add from your side?
[00:25] Maria: Procurement mostly wants to understand the commercial lanes and who signs off. Also egress fees for financial data are a big thing for us.
[00:28] Leo: (observer) we'll be looking at cost sensitivity, yep.
[00:31] Jin: Legal is focused on DPA addenda, subprocessor list, and also whether we can get customer-managed keys and audit logs for every request.
[00:38] Samir (SE): Great — I'll show typical architecture options and what changes on the SLA/KMS front between hosted and dedicated.
[00:45] Alex: Cool, Samir take it away.
[00:48] Samir: Ok, so at a high level Redwood offers hosted API — that's quickest — and dedicated pools which give you reserved GPU capacity. For Stargazer, two tradeoffs: hosted is lower friction and lower initial commit, dedicated gives you predictable throughput and stronger isolation. Latency SLOs depend on model choice and batching; we can hit p95 < 150ms on smaller LLMs, for larger long-context models you should expect higher.
[01:12] Tara (Customer): Could you clarify "small" vs "large" LLMs? We run a mix — some rerankers and a 32k context model for document summarization.
[01:20] Samir: Yeah sorry fuzzy language — e.g., 7B-ish models and cacheable rerankers are the low latency path; 30B+ autoregressive with long context will be higher and we see more variance. For large context workloads we recommend dedicated with KV cache pinning.
[01:35] Jin: Is KV pinning something in the public hosted API or only on dedicated?
[01:38] Samir: We have prefix/KV caching in hosted but customer-level pinning and per-tenant opaque caching controls are part of Dedicated / Private deployment. The hosted product gives automated prefix caching but not customer-managed KV persistence.
[01:50] Maria: From procurement point, committed spend for Dedicated — what are typical tiers?
[01:54] Alex: We have monthly reserved pools starting at a modest capacity tier (like 10k tokens per minute equivalent) up to enterprise pools. Pricing is structured as base monthly commit + per-token overage, and you get discount tiers for annual commitment. I'll send the spreadsheet.
[02:09] Maria: And egress? How do you charge inter-region egress or data egress for model outputs?
[02:14] Alex: Standard is we bill for network egress if we host your data in a different region than the consumer access. For most customers egress is minimal, but if you require strict data residency we recommend Redwood Private (VPC) or a dedicated region deployment to avoid cross-region egress fees.
[02:29] Jin: About keys — we need customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM. Is that supported on hosted?
[02:34] Samir: Hosted supports server-side encryption and we integrate with cloud KMS for our keys; customer-managed KMS is available for Dedicated and Private where you can provide a key in your tenant. On hosted we can evaluate a bring-your-own-key (BYOK) path but it has more constraints and is typically an enterprise add-on.
[02:50] Jin: And audit logs for every request — can we get request-level logs filtered for PII? We need per-request traceability.
[02:56] Samir: Yes we produce audit logs with request metadata, latency, token counts. We can also mask PII at ingestion with transformations, but that requires configuration. For Private deployments you get full request logs shipped to your SIEM. For hosted we can deliver logs to a secure bucket or SIEM integration with restricted retention.
[03:15] Tara: About the SLA itself — what's the uptime and credit model?
[03:18] Alex: Our Dedicated SLAs aim for 99.95% monthly uptime for reserved pools; hosted SLA is lower for free tiers but enterprise hosted customers can get SLA addendums. Credits are pro-rata based on downtime; also we give routes for automatic fallback to a lower-capacity model if the primary model is unavailable.
[03:36] Jin: Can we get the SLA language in the MSA? We need explicit remedies for outages impacting our production.
[03:40] Alex: Absolutely — we'll include SLA wording in the MSA sample. We'll flag the specific downtime credit language.
[03:45] Maria: One JIRA-ish question — for onboarding who needs to be involved? Engineering, procurement, legal? Any typical timeline?
[03:51] Alex: Usually it's SE-led kickoff, 2-week pilot for functionality and perf, then procurement/legal for MSA/DPA. For a pilot + procurement cycle, typical timeline is 4-8 weeks depending on redlines. If you want accelerated path we can run contract review parallel to a non-prod pilot.
[04:07] Jin: On DPA: we have a list of required clauses — subprocessor audit, deletion timelines, data residency specifics. We may ask for specific redlines around deletion windows.
[04:16] Samir: Deletion and retention are configurable — hosted default is 30 days for request artifacts but we can negotiate retention in the DPA and for Private you can set retention to your policy. We also support data classification tags to route sensitive traffic to Private pools.
[04:32] Maria: Are you SOC 2 Type II? We need evidence for our infosec.
[04:36] Alex: Yes, Redwood is SOC 2 Type II. I will attach the report redacted to exclude vendor-specific material. We'll also provide the subprocessor list.
[04:45] Jin: Can you enumerate subprocessors and whether any are offshore? We have a requirement around that.
[04:49] Alex: We'll include the subprocessors and territories in the pack. Most infra providers are cloud hyperscalers; we can flag any that have data processing in regions you flag.
[04:58] Tara: For the pilot, what telemetry do you need from us? We'll run sample prompts and a couple of production-like queries.
[05:05] Samir: If you can provide a representative prompt set, expected concurrency, token distribution, and a sample of 32k-context documents, we'll populate the benchmark harness. Also any latency SLOs you care about (p50/p95 targets).
[05:16] Maria: On pricing — if we commit to a 12 month reserved pool, what discounts do we see versus pay-as-you-go?
[05:22] Alex: Typical discounts vary by commit level; small reserved commitments may get 15-25% off token unit price, larger enterprise commits can be more. We can model a couple of scenarios — I'll attach a sensitivity sheet.
[05:34] Leo: Do you charge for KV cache storage for pinned caches?
[05:37] Samir: There's a small monthly fee for persistent KV on Dedicated/Private; the economics are captured in the committed pool pricing model.
[05:44] Jin: Any export control or compliance flags we should know for financial data?
[05:48] Alex: We do support data residency+governance controls; we also have a compliance team that can do a walkthrough if you need deeper controls. Export controls vary by jurisdiction; we'll surface any constraints for the regions you operate in.
[05:59] Maria: Ok, sounds good. Can you also include the process for rolling model updates and regression monitoring? We need to avoid quality regressions after model upgrades.
[06:08] Samir: We do staged rollouts: canary, A/B, auto-fallback; plus Redwood Optimize includes quality monitoring and eval hooks. We'll document the rollback paths and alerting.
[06:20] Alex: Quick note — you mentioned Anthropic/OpenAI, right? Many customers benchmark across providers; Redwood's differentiator here is predictable serving and rollback policies plus dedicated/private options.
[06:31] Jin: Any intellectual property carve-outs? We're concerned about model training on our data.
[06:35] Alex: Redwood does not use customer data to train our models unless explicitly agreed in the contract. We'll put that in the DPA/MSA language.
[06:44] Maria: Great. Let's quickly recap the blockers: 1) DPA redlines around retention and subprocessors, 2) KMS/BYOK path and audit logs, 3) pricing sensitivity and egress concerns. Anything else?
[06:56] Tara: Also technical validation for 32k context throughput.
[06:59] Alex: Perfect. For next steps: I'll send pricing + MSA sample; Samir will send benchmark template; Jin you'll share DPA details; Maria you'll confirm internal approvers and volume.
[07:12] Jin: Sounds good. Thank you.
[07:14] Maria: Thanks everyone.
[07:16] Alex: Thanks all — we'll follow up over email.

(End of recording)
